text.p: Several insurance companies, including a foreign group, are interested in taking part in the upcoming privatisation of Italian motorway operator Autostrade, Italian press reports said.

Apart from the Benetton group's Edizione holding, which has already confirmed its interest, other potential bidders include Italian insurers Generali and Ras, daily La Repubblica said without citing sources.
Business daily Il Sole 24 Ore also speculated a group of Veneto region-based partners could make a bid for a sizeable stake via the northeastern Banca Antoniana Veneta.

La Repubblica valued one percent of Autostrade at around 40 billion lire, noting that potential shareholders could not have interests in transport or construction and would be restricted to a maximum three percent stake.
It said a foreign insurance company "probably Japanese" was also interested in taking a stake.
The sale of Autostrade, which is 87 percent owned by state industrial holding IRI, is due to take place by the end of June.
